Coverage guard: 2 gap(s); corrective re-draft...

- Uncovered claim 'The decline was driven by accelerated pipeline decay' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts a causal relationship: the coverage decline was caused by accelerated pipeline decay. AC4 and AC5 both use stage_aging but only measure the absolute share of stale opportunities (max_stale_share_pct), not the acceleration of decay over time. No existing criterion measures the trend/acceleration of aging that would prove decay was 'accelerated' rather than merely present. The stage_aging check as drafted cannot distinguish acceleration from a static high stale share. (consider check: stage_aging)

- Uncovered claim 'Once stale opportunities were removed, effective coverage was materially lower than reported' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim requires that effective coverage (after removing stale opportunities) be materially LOWER than reported coverage. AC6 checks coverage_ratio with min_multiple 2.0 for FY26-Q2, but this only verifies coverage is at least 2.0x — it does not compare effective coverage against reported coverage. The claim's substance is a relative comparison (effective < reported), which no existing criterion expresses. A coverage_ratio check can only confirm an absolute threshold, not the differential between adjusted and reported figures. (consider check: coverage_ratio)

[note] Uncovered claim 'The decline was driven by accelerated pipeline decay' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts a causal relationship: the coverage decline was caused by accelerated pipeline decay (stale opportunities). The stage_aging check can measure the share of opportunities aging beyond the threshold, but no existing check expresses the causal linkage between decay acceleration and the coverage decline. AC4 and AC5 measure stale-share magnitude but not that decay drove the decline. The substance (causal attribution) is not measurable by any single existing check's parameters. (consider check: stage_aging)

[note] Uncovered claim 'Once stale opportunities were removed, effective coverage was materially lower than reported' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim requires comparing effective coverage (stale removed) against reported coverage and asserting effective is materially lower. The coverage_ratio check measures a single coverage multiple against a min_multiple threshold but cannot express the relative comparison between two coverage definitions (effective vs reported). AC6 and AC7 both check FY26-Q2 coverage against absolute thresholds (2.9 and 2.0) but neither captures the 'lower than reported' differential. The substance (relative reduction from removing stale) is not expressible by coverage_ratio's parameters. (consider check: coverage_ratio)

- Uncovered claim 'The decline was driven by accelerated pipeline decay' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts a causal relationship: the coverage decline was caused by accelerated pipeline decay (stale opportunities leaving the pipeline). The existing checks AC4 and AC5 measure the level of stale share but do not measure the trend in decay/slippage that would prove the decline was 'driven by' decay rather than by coverage numerator/denominator composition changes. slippage_trend can express accelerating decay over the quarter, but no drafted criterion invokes it. The causal attribution is the substance of this claim and is not captured by the level-based stage_aging checks. (consider check: slippage_trend)

- Uncovered claim 'Once stale opportunities were removed, effective coverage was materially lower than reported' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim compares effective coverage (after removing stale opportunities) against reported coverage and requires effective to be materially lower. The drafted AC6 uses forecast_vs_actual, which measures forecast accuracy (target_pct 109, band 5pp) rather than the reported-vs-effective coverage gap. coverage_ratio is the correct primitive to express effective vs reported coverage, but no criterion measures the effective-coverage shortfall. forecast_vs_actual does not measure the same entity/metric and its parameters (forecast overachievement) do not correspond to the claim's substance. (consider check: coverage_ratio)

A criterion that proves this claim would need to confirm the decay is the dominant driver of the coverage decline, not merely that decay increased. The existing slippage_trend check can express decay acceleration but cannot verify the causal 'driven by' substance that ties decay magnitude to the coverage decline.
